Source: Ivory Homes press release: Ivory Homes and Larry H. Miller Communities lead community vision for master-planned community in eastern Summit County
Research note: A landowner-partnership model: the land stays with the owners while Ivory and LHM entitle and develop.

Description: Ivory Development is the applicant for the 'Lost Creek' project on Browns Canyon Road on behalf of LLCs tied to the Garff and Rogers families, who own the land: a county rezone covering about 600 acres (about 400 developed, 2,300 to 3,000 homes) and a parallel state application to form a town (510 units on 491 acres). The planning commission gave a negative recommendation in August 2026; the county council had not yet scheduled it as of October 2026.
Source: KPCW: Ivory Homes reactivates effort to make Browns Canyon town
Research note: Whether Ivory holds an option or purchase contract on the land is not stated in the coverage.

Partner: Call to Action Foundation (with Ivory Innovations)
Description: 'Call to Innovation' philanthropic partnership between Ivory Innovations, the Ivory family's housing foundation, and the Call to Action Foundation, aiming to build 1,500 affordable homes in Utah; projects include Innovation Park at Francis Commons, inside a master plan Ivory Homes is developing, and Innovation Park at Holbrook Farms in Lehi on land donated by Ivory Homes.
Source: Utah Business press release: Ivory Innovations brings affordable housing to Summit County
Research note: Philanthropic, not a financing source for the for-sale business; shows Ivory carving land out of its own master plans.

Description: McGuinn sells homes to BTR capital groups as an 'active Build-to-Rent partner'; trade press says BTR at times made up most of its business. No investor is named.
Source: PR Newswire: Privately-Held Homebuilder Poised for Regional Growth (McGuinn Homes Inc.)
Research note: Not a JV in the formal sense; recorded here because it is the main outside-capital relationship. 'Bulk of business' is Reported by ResiClub (2026-07-08).

Description: University Village Holdings LLC, a joint venture between the master planner The Rector Cos. and HHHunt, was the borrower on a $58M HUD-insured construction loan arranged by Berkadia for the 336-unit Abberly Avera apartments near Manassas, VA.
Source: Berkadia arranges $58 million construction loan for apartments (Virginia Business)
Research note: Seen in search snippet only, not confirmed: the Virginia Business page returned 403. Older, apartment-side deal; it shows HHHunt has used a landowner / master-planner joint venture at least once. Abberly Avera is still listed on HHHunt's Virginia page.

Description: Mortgage arrangement, not a land venture: 'View Homes Lending' is a division (dba) of NFM Lending, which discloses a financial relationship with View Homes. Listed here only so the mortgage partner is on record.
Source: View Homes Lending site footer disclosure

Partner: J.H. Berra Construction (as Elite Development; also seen as McBride Berra Land Co)
Description: Land-development joint venture with the St. Louis site contractor J.H. Berra: the venture buys and develops ground and McBride builds on it. In Dec 2020 it closed on 10 acres in Affton for a 44-lot subdivision.
Source: St. Louis Call Newspapers: McBride buys land for subdivision in Affton
Research note: Only source opened is from Dec 2020. Search snippets of later St. Louis Business Journal items (via KSDK, pages blocked) show 'McBride Berra Land Co' and 'Elite Development' filing subdivision plans in Wildwood, Florissant and south St. Louis County, so the venture appears to continue, but its current status and terms are unconfirmed.

Description: Master developer agreement (a public-private arrangement, not an equity joint venture) for the 144.5-acre former Jamestown Mall site: 700+ homes, about 11 acres of retail, 38+ acres of amenities.
Source: McBride Homes press release: McBride Homes to Redevelop Former Jamestown Mall Site

Description: Public-private partnership for Progress Pointe (137 homes): the city funds subdivision infrastructure through a $10 million bond initiative; McBride builds and sells the homes.
Source: McBride Homes press release: McBride Homes Celebrates Groundbreaking of Progress Pointe in Ste. Genevieve

Description: McBride and the grocer Dierbergs together bought the 47-acre former Crestwood Mall site (closed 2022-01-26) and redeveloped it as Crestwood Crossing: homes by McBride, a grocery store and retail.
Source: REjournals: Sansone helps close deal to turn former mall in St. Louis market into mixed-use development
Research note: Source is from Jan 2022. McBride's Oct 2026 Jamestown release still cites Crestwood Crossing as its own redevelopment, but Dierbergs' continuing ownership role is not confirmed by a newer source.

Description: Three-builder joint venture for the master-planned Reserve at Lakeview Farms in St. Charles; McBride took 35 homesites in phase 1.
Source: McBride Homes press release: New Community in St. Charles off Towers Road Set to Open in March
Research note: Company release from Feb 2022; shown as evidence that McBride shares land with other local builders. Current status of the venture is not confirmed.

Description: Joint-venture mortgage company, HomeKey Mortgage, LLC, formed May 2023 to finance McBride's buyers. This is homebuyer mortgage lending, not land or corporate finance.
Source: McBride Homes press release: McBride Homes and Golden Oak Lending Announce Joint Venture Mortgage Company
Research note: The live financing page (retrieved 2026-11-19) still names HomeKey Mortgage as McBride's preferred lender.

Partner: City of McAllen and Hidalgo County (Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone No. 1 and the Tres Lagos Public Improvement District)
Description: Public-private structure for Tres Lagos: the city approved a TIRZ agreement with Rhodes Enterprises in March 2015, with the county contributing part of its tax increment, to reimburse public infrastructure. The city said Rhodes would invest over $232M in public infrastructure across a 30-year build-out of the 2,571-acre plan. A public improvement district administers and helps fund the development.
Source: City of McAllen news release: City moves forward with Tres Lagos development
Research note: The 2016 amended and restated interlocal agreement (Hidalgo County record, re-posted with a 2026-01-27 county agenda) requires the developer to post an annually renewed irrevocable letter of credit equal to each year's debt service on the city's master-infrastructure certificates of obligation until tax increment covers 120% of that debt service. Current status of the letter of credit and of the 2026 agenda item was not confirmed.

Description: Ironcrest Mortgage, LLC: mortgage-lending joint venture for Stone Martin buyers in Alabama, office at 1799 Ogletree Road, Auburn. Not a land venture.
Source: Cornerstone Bank and Stone Martin Builders Launch Ironcrest Mortgage Across Alabama (company blog)
Research note: The company's March 2026 post also mentions a title-services venture without naming a partner.

Description: Wakefield Development says it has joined projects along the East Coast as a silent partner, a side-by-side partner and a land-development partner, and will take over stalled projects. No specific JV partner or deal is named.
Source: Wakefield Development - Opportunities
Research note: Generic capability statement, not a specific JV.

Description: River Crossing: eight income-qualified townhomes at 100 West 600 South, Logan, built by Visionary on land donated by the city and sold by lottery to buyers below area median income. A public-private partnership rather than a capital joint venture.
Source: Visionary Homes and City of Logan Break Ground on River Crossing (company press release)

Description: Seven Pines partnership, Jacksonville: the two builders jointly bought and are developing the Skinner family's last large tract (about 550 acres; about 1,600 homes plus apartments and commercial) and both build in it. Mori Hosseini is the managing partner of the partnership. Nearly 500 homes had sold by Dec 2025.
Source: ICI Homes / David Weekley Homes press release: ICI Homes and David Weekley Homes Acquire Skinner Family Property (as carried by What's Up Jacksonville)
Research note: Still current: a Feb 2026 ICI release again calls Hosseini the managing partner of Seven Pines. Ownership split, entity name and any project debt are not public.

Description: Long-running programmatic JV. 2018 press-release boilerplate said Presidio funds 100 percent of SJV Homes' projects and operations and that Presidio is affiliated with an unnamed privately held registered investment adviser; by April 2024 the partners counted 40 communities. Presidio principal Paul Lucatuorto is listed as Co-CEO of SJV Homes on the builder's team page (modified 2026-10-20).
Source: Press release on Construction Dive: SJV Homes and Presidio open sales at Brighton (2018-08-13)
Research note: The 100 percent funding statement is from 2018 and has not been restated recently. SJV Homes' own boilerplate named Presidio in February 2024 but names only Joe Leal and Randy Merrill from February 2025 through November 2026, and communities opened in 2025-2026 (Andalusia, Blossom Hill, Somerset, Sorrento, Andover Place, Danbury Estates) were announced without a named capital partner. Whether the JV terms, the funding share or ownership changed is not publicly disclosed; the Co-CEO listing argues the relationship continues.

Description: Presidio's site lists preferred project lenders (Bank of the West/BNP Paribas, First Security Bank, Farmers & Merchants Bank, HomeStreet Bank, Torrey Bank, U.S. Bank), and a Farmers & Merchants Bank testimonial cites more than $100M of loans secured by Presidio projects over two years. None is tied publicly to a specific SJV Homes community.
Source: Presidio Residential Capital: Preferred Lenders page and testimonials page (undated)
Research note: Indicative only: shows that Presidio-funded projects do carry bank project debt; which lenders hold SJV Homes project loans is not publicly disclosed. Testimonial source: https://www.presidioresidential.com/testimonials/

Description: NHC Mortgage, a joint-venture mortgage company serving National HomeCorp buyers, launched in Florida, Iowa and North Carolina with more states planned for 2023. This is a buyer-financing venture, not land or construction capital. The company's financing page still discloses an ownership interest in NHC Mortgage as a joint venture.
Source: loanDepot press release: loanDepot and National HomeCorp launch NHC Mortgage
Research note: Current ownership disclosure seen on nationalhomecorp.com/financing (retrieved 2026-11-19); that page does not name loanDepot, so the partner today is confirmed only as of the 2022 release.

Partner: Network Partners, LLC (affiliate of Network Funding, LP)
Description: Colina Mortgage Group, LLC, the builder's 'preferred lender', is a mortgage joint venture: Texas records list its two members as Network Partners LLC and Nuway Holdings LLC (Ken Williams's holding company), with its mailing address at Colina's office. This is buyer mortgage origination, not land or construction finance.
Source: Texas Comptroller franchise tax account status: Colina Mortgage Group, LLC (2026 report year)
Research note: Registered with the Texas Secretary of State 2019-07-22; active. The Network Funding link is inferred: Network Partners, LLC's officers are Gregory Baker (President) and Rex Chamberlain (CEO) at 10370 Richmond Ave, Suite 900, Houston (https://comptroller.texas.gov/data-search/franchise-tax/32075736432), the headquarters address Network Funding, LP publishes, and Network Funding's about page names Rex Chamberlain (https://www.nflp.com/about). Colina's site names Colina Mortgage Group as preferred lender at https://www.colinahomes.com/lets-get-started.

Description: Westford Glen, Henrico County, VA: Schell Brothers assembled about 76 acres (nine parcels, under contract) and brought in Midlothian-based Main Street Homes as co-developer. Rezoning sought for up to 330 townhomes and 40 detached homes plus 3 commercial acres; Main Street's president put the cost at about $175M at buildout, with construction roughly two years out and a four-year buildout. County staff had not yet backed the rezoning in Nov 2025. The two builders also work together on Dogwood Creek in Chesterfield.
Source: Developer duo planning 350-plus homes beside closed landfill near Wyndham (Richmond BizSense)
Research note: Ownership split and legal structure not described. No lender or capital partner named: a large, infrastructure-heavy site with no announced funding. Rezoning outcome after Nov 2025 not checked.

Description: StillCroft, Ashland, VA: a 26-home gated community on roughly 6-acre lots that Schell Brothers developed together with the agent.
Source: Schell Brothers planning 68-home subdivision west of Harpers Mill (Richmond BizSense)
Research note: Small; structure not described.

Description: Park Square Home Mortgage (PSH Mortgage, NMLS 1683180) is a joint venture between Park Square Homes and FBC Mortgage; it funds buyer incentives such as builder-paid forward-commitment rate buydowns.
Source: Family of Companies (company site)
Research note: Buyer mortgage JV, not land finance.

Description: Kimaya Management Group, a JV between Kimaya and Atrium Management, manages Kimaya's build-to-rent communities and some multifamily assets; Park Square Homes was general contractor on Kimaya's Ocoee Village build-to-rent townhomes (AAGO 'Build To Rent Community of the Year', January 2026).
Source: Kimaya Family of Companies
Research note: Ocoee Village award: https://www.parksquarehomes.com/blog/ocoee-village-townhome-awarded-build-to-rent-community-of-the-year/

Description: Kimaya, the commercial real-estate affiliate in the Park Square family of companies, develops multifamily, build-to-rent and other commercial projects ($500M+ total development cost of portfolio, per its About page) and works with family offices, registered investment advisors, fund managers, institutional investors and select high-net-worth individuals (Investor Relations page).
Source: Kimaya About Us
Research note: Investor relations page: https://kimayarealestate.com/investor-relations/ . No named investor or lender. Verification 2026-11-19: 'formed in 2015' and 'subsidiary of Park Square Enterprises' are not stated on the About or Investor Relations pages and were removed from the description.
